headline: Four days out and the final quiet holds. Strength stayed live right up to the edge, legs are fresh, engine banked. Everything from here is the trail itself.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is a clean pre-event trough, not a fade. Running has dropped to short, easy shakeouts sitting almost entirely in the lowest zone, which is exactly what you want with the crossing imminent — the 71% four-week build already banked the durability, and these last runs are just keeping the legs turning. Strength is the standout thread: the session two weeks running kept the streak alive into its eighth week and held load right to the taper's edge rather than dropping it early. Steps remain genuinely high even as running volume falls, so background load and time on feet haven't collapsed the way the "detraining" strain readout implies. That flag reads the recent quiet literally; it doesn't see the base underneath it. Recovery nights are the one unsettled variable, but they don't change the readiness verdict this close to the start.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is a deliberate build-then-taper into a defined event, which is a departure from the athlete's usual year-round non-periodised rhythm — and appropriately so, given a 580 km self-supported crossing. Year-to-date, the distance gap versus last year is enormous, which tells you the aerobic base under this taper is far deeper than the recent weekly numbers alone suggest. The current dip isn't a plateau or drift; it's the intended low point before a very long, sustained block of loaded time on feet takes over.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchoring HR are unchanged over the baseline window, which is precisely what you'd expect through a taper — you don't sharpen threshold this close in, you protect it. The relevant read isn't whether threshold is improving right now but that it's intact and stable heading into an event where raw speed matters far less than repeatable aerobic economy under a pack. The engine is where it needs to be.
sections.zones: The recent per-session shapes are textbook taper: the last several runs sit almost wholly in Z1 with brief Z2 touches and no meaningful Z3+ time, a deliberate contrast to the genuinely hard mixed session late in July that carried real Z3 and Z4 minutes. That earlier run confirms top-end was present when the block wanted it; the recent flatness confirms it's been correctly switched off. For what these final days are trying to do — arrive fresh — the distribution is right.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing concerning in the strength or run HR patterns. The strength sessions sit low and steady, consistent with functional maintenance work rather than metabolically taxing efforts, and where run HR is present it tracks pace sensibly. No source-agreement issue worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The calendar shows the frequency deliberately thinning as the event nears — strength held to a steady cadence while running compressed into short doubles on the final active days. That's a controlled wind-down, not an erratic gap. The consistency of the strength thread through the taper is the genuinely notable part: it's the one modality that never got fully parked.
sections.personal_bests: No PBs are in play here and none should be — the training focus has been durability and banked base, not sharpening for a fast time trial. The speed bests from last autumn remain the reference point for a future speed-oriented block, not this one.

watch_items: Watch how "easy" HR behaves once consecutive loaded days begin — the first few days will reset what easy actually costs under a pack.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under load is still the real unknown, not the engine.
Note how the border mountain crossing sits within the daily rhythm — read that terrain spike separately from the flatter sections.
Watch whether recovery nights steady once the trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.
